items.title: Selangor seeks legal advice on assemblyman's status, possible by-election
items.summary: news@nst.com.my KUALA PILAH: The Selangor government is reviewing claims that a state assemblyman has lost his eligibility to remain in office. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the state government had received preliminary information on the matter and was seeking legal advice before deciding on further action, including whether a by-election would be required. He said the issue was expected to be raised during the state assembly sitting scheduled for Oct 3.

items.title: #NSTviral: 28-time blood donor inspires Malaysians with message
items.summary: Known only as Vince, the man shared on Threads that he had donated blood 28 times, with each donation involving 450ml of blood. The doctor replied, 'because your blood matches the blood of a Malay child with thalassaemia'," he said. "My blood has never known Malay, Chinese or Indian.

items.title: PH confident of keeping Negri Sembilan with 22-seat target
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Pakatan Harapan is confident of retaining power in Negri Sembilan, with a target of winning between 21 and 22 of the 36 seats up for grabs in the state election. PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the target was achievable based on voters' ability to evaluate PH's performance since 2018, as well as the two-term administration record of Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun. "2018 was PH's best year when we won 20 seats.

items.title: Iranian army says drones target key US facilities at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base
items.summary: MANAMA, (Bahrain): Iran's army said Thursday it targeted key US military facilities at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base with one-way attack drones amid an exchange of attacks between Teheran and Washington across the West Asia region, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported. It said the drones struck power generators, navigation systems and administrative and support buildings used by what it described as the US military at Sheikh Isa Air Base. The military claimed that repeated attacks on US bases in the region over recent days had inflicted "significant damage" on military equipment and facilities despite the bases being protected by multiple air defence systems.

items.title: BOJ to keep rates steady, deliver hawkish signal as government props up yen
items.summary: TOKYO: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) is set to keep interest rates steady on Friday but signal its resolve to continue pushing up borrowing costs, after the government intervened to boost the weak yen, keeping pressure on the central bank to show its hawkishness. Having just raised rates in June, the BOJ is widely expected to keep short-term interest rates steady at one per cent. Hawkish board member Hajime Takata may dissent and propose a hike to 1.25 per cent, some analysts say.

items.title: South Korea conducts rare dollar-selling intervention, source says
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korea's foreign exchange authorities conducted a rare dollar-selling intervention on Thursday, sending the won to a nine-month high, a market source told Reuters on Friday. Seoul's move came alongside Japan's yen-buying, dollar-selling market intervention in New York markets on Thursday, pulling the yen from four-decade lows. "Foreign exchange officials conducted rare dollar-selling intervention overnight," the source said, declining to be identified.

items.title: AI spending boom could be market's biggest risk: Franklin Income CIO
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The capital expenditure (capex) needed around artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure could be a key risk in markets going into the second half of the year. Franklin Income Investors chief investment officer Ed Perks said data centre and large infrastructure projects are drawing on similar resources and competing for capital at the same time. This creates the potential for bottlenecks as companies pursue massive buildouts, Perks said.

items.title: Karnival Jom Heboh Sarawak Segulai Sejalai 2026 begins today
items.summary: KOTA SAMARAHAN: Karnival Jom Heboh (KJH) has returned to Sarawak, with the three-day Karnival Jom Heboh Sarawak Segulai Sejalai 2026 beginning today and running until Sunday at the Kota Samarahan Municipal Council grounds. Organised by Media Prima Bhd in strategic collaboration with the Sarawak Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Ministry (MTCP), the carnival also provides visitors with the opportunity to engage with various agencies under the ministry through exhibitions, activities and initiatives held throughout the event. Following the encouraging response to its inaugural edition last year, the Jom Heboh Fun Run returns for a second year, promising participants an even more exciting experience.

items.title: Gold rises on weaker US dollar, soft inflation data
items.summary: NEW YORK: Gold rose on Thursday as the US dollar weakened and inflation eased, with traders dialling back bets on interest rate hikes a day after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh offered little clarity on policy. Spot gold was up one per cent at US$4,104.59 per ounce by 1:40 p.m. EDT (1740 GMT). US gold futures for August delivery gained 1.60 per cent to settle at US$4,160.60.

items.title: Oil settles down on proposed Saudi-led maritime defence coalition
items.summary: NEW YORK: Oil prices settled lower on Thursday after a volatile session, as traders digested proposed plans for a Saudi Arabia-led maritime coalition to boost defence cooperation around the Red Sea. Brent futures settled down US$1.71, or 1.88 per cent, at US$89.03 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures settled down 87 cents, or 1.03 per cent, at US$83.59, after hitting a high of US$85.94.

items.title: TH RCI a lesson in governance failure, voters told
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Governance and integrity should be the key considerations for voters in the 16th Negri Sembilan election to prevent further erosion of the nation's institutions through corruption and abuse of power, says Pakatan Harapan (PH) communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Referring to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), he said its findings should serve as a reminder of the consequences of weak governance and abuse of power. "The commission's findings have been referred to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) for further action," he said at a PH ceramah in the Senaling state constituency tonight.

items.title: Tabung Haji's buyback of Urusharta Jamaah assets based on commercial value, not obligation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji says its recent repurchase of selected assets from Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd reflects a disciplined investment strategy and should not be viewed as a reversal of its 2018 restructuring programme. Under the restructuring exercise, Urusharta Jamaah - a government-owned special purpose vehicle - bought underperforming and problematic Tabung Haji assets to help eliminate a financial deficit that had exceeded RM10 billion. Under the restructuring, assets with a carrying value of RM9.7 billion were sold to Urusharta for RM19.9 billion.

items.title: Microsoft sets record with near US$450bil single-day gain in market value
items.summary: NEW YORK: Microsoft added nearly US$450 billion in market value on Thursday, the largest one-day gain on record for a company, after it forecast stronger-than-expected cloud growth and signalled continued cash generation through its new fiscal year. The software giant's shares closed up more than 15 per cent, lifting its market capitalisation to US$3.35 trillion, surpassing chip giant Nvidia's previous record one-day gain of US$441 billion on April 9, 2025, according to LSEG data. Microsoft said its spending plans remain unchanged and that it expects capital expenditures of US$50 billion for the fiscal first quarter of 2027 and US$175 billion for the 2026 calendar year.

items.title: Why Tabung Haji's 2018 restructuring was unavoidable
items.summary: Tabung Haji, in a statement today, said concerns over its financial position had been building for several years. The Auditor General's 2017 financial report also highlighted accounting practices that did not accurately reflect Tabung Haji's true financial position. Tabung Haji said without urgent intervention it would not have met the requirements of the Tabung Haji Act to declare any profit distribution.

items.title: Tabung Haji completes financial turnaround, overcomes RM12.6bil in investment losses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji says it has restored its financial strength following a comprehensive recovery and restructuring programme launched in 2018. The recovery plan had addressed RM12.6 billion in investment losses, comprising RM10 billion through the 2018 restructuring and a further RM2.6 billion progressively until the end of 2025. This had positioned it for long-term sustainability and improved returns for depositors, Tabung Haji said in a statement today.

items.title: When trust is broken
items.summary: TRUST is one of the most valuable assets in any workplace. Once trust has been broken, however, rebuilding it is neither quick nor easy. Rebuilding trust requires genuine remorse, consistent action, patience, and a commitment to personal growth.

items.title: Wall Street ends sharply higher, lifted by soaring Microsoft
items.summary: Microsoft jumped over 15 per cent, boosting its stock market value by US$450 billion, the greatest-ever single-day increase for a company on Wall Street. The PHLX chip index surged 8.20 per cent, with Micron Technology jumping 18 per cent, Sandisk soaring 26 per cent and Advanced Micro Devices up 13 per cent. Amazon rose 3.90 per cent and Apple dipped 1.40 per cent, with both companies set to report their results after the market closes.

items.title: Maybank: A new home for a six-decade institution [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: After more than six decades at the heart of the capital's old financial district, Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) is turning the page on its history. The country's biggest bank has moved its headquarters into the landmark Menara Merdeka Maybank as it positions itself for the next chapter of growth. "Since its establishment in 1960, Maybank has grown alongside Malaysia's development.

items.title: Bursa raises IPO target to RM34bil as Q2 earnings jump 26pct [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia Bhd, which posted a 25.9 per cent increase in second-quarter earnings, has raised its initial public offering (IPO) market capitalisation target for 2026 to RM34 billion, backed by a robust listing pipeline. Net profit for the quarter ended June 30 increased to RM71.78 million from RM57.06 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 22.3 per cent to RM210.97 million from RM172.58 million. For the first half of 2026, net profit increased 15.2 per cent to RM144.61 million from RM125.48 million in the corresponding period last year, while revenue grew 19.1 per cent to RM425.04 million from RM356.78 million.

items.title: Milei demands expulsion of foreigners expressing 'hate' against Argentina
items.summary: BUENOS AIRES: Argentine President Javier Milei on Thursday imposed a bar on foreigners who express "hate" towards the Latin American country, which he claims is the target of a sinister campaign. In a statement, Milei said the measure was in response to "recent displays of hostility against the Argentine Republic and Argentines". The ultraliberal leader appeared to be referring to public reactions to Argentina's recent World Cup final loss against Spain.

items.title: BN-PN 'alliance' faces litmus test
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan voters will head to the polls tomorrow to decide who governs the state for the next five years, but the outcome could have ramifications beyond its borders. Beyond deciding the composition of the 36-seat state assembly, the election will test whether Barisan Nasional's electoral understanding with the Pas-led Perikatan Nasional can deliver results. PH is contesting all 36 seats, while BN and PN have avoided three-cornered fights by dividing the constituencies between themselves, with BN fielding candidates in 25 seats and PN in the remaining 11.

items.title: Trump announces agreement on disarmament of Hamas, Israeli withdrawal from Gaza
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that an agreement had been reached for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza, with Israeli forces set to withdraw as the process moves forward, Anadolu Ajansi reported. Trump said the deal, which he described as a "historic" step towards peace and security, would be carried out in phases. As disarmament is completed, Israeli forces will withdraw, and the International Stabilisation Force will work with a new Palestinian police force to take responsibility for Gaza being safe for its residents and its neighbours," he wrote in a post on his social media platform Truth Social.

items.title: Brazilian Supreme Court justice authorises investigation into president's son
items.summary: SAO PAULO: Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Andre Mendonca has authorised federal police to investigate Fabio Luis Lula da Silva, son of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, over suspicions he improperly helped a lobbyist in dealings with the health ministry, two sources with direct knowledge of the decision told Reuters. Last week, federal police sought permission to open an investigation into Fabio Luis, known as "Lulinha", for alleged influence peddling and corruption on behalf of Antonio Carlos Camilo Antunes in dealings with the ministry. The investigation into Fabio Luis has not yet been formally opened, a federal police source said.

items.title: 'RCI shows govt's resolve in restoring trust in Tabung Haji' [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Tabung Haji has uncovered governance lapses and underscored the government's resolve to restore institutional integrity and accountability. Putra Business School eco-nomist Professor Dr Ahmed Razman Abdul Latiff said the findings reflected the government's willingness to confront past failures, hold institutions to account and strengthen safeguards against future misconduct. [[nid:1500943]] On the potential impact on public confidence, Razman said depositor trust would depend on whether governance reforms continued to be implemented effectively.

items.title: A fresh start: Teksi Madani policy looks at uplifting taxi drivers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — For many of Malaysia’s ageing taxi drivers, dwindling passengers are only part of the problem. The programme combines tax exemptions, rebates, easier financing and direct permit ownership to help drivers replace ageing taxis, lower the barriers to ownership and modernise the industry. Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the programme was inspired not merely by statistics, but by what he repeatedly witnessed during constituency programmes with taxi drivers.

items.title: Nepal PM urges calm after unrest leaves 3 dead
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Thursday appealed for calm after clashes between Hindu and Muslim groups in the country's south sparked unrest that has left three people dead. Police opened fire to disperse the crowd, said local official Poshan Lamichhane. Two men died in the unrest, according to police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle.

items.title: Blast at Pakistan coal mine complex kills at least 11, dozens missing
items.summary: QUETTA: At least 11 coal miners were killed and dozens are missing after an explosion buried parts of a mining complex in Pakistan's Balochistan province on Thursday, an official said. Of them, 25 were missing late on Thursday night, he said. Abdul Ghani Baloch, a senior government mining official in the region, said: "Two mines close to each other were damaged in a powerful methane gas explosion."

items.title: Saudi sets up maritime defence alliance to secure Red Sea
items.summary: RIYADH: Saudi Arabia said on Thursday it had set up a maritime defence alliance to secure navigation around the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. The move comes after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said last week they were imposing a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia, the world's top oil exporter, and claimed attacks targeting Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and oil infrastructure in the kingdom. The Saudi defence ministry issued a joint statement on behalf of the 14 countries in the alliance: Bahrain, Bangladesh, Djibouti, Egypt, Jordan, Kuwait, Nigeria, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Sudan, Turkiye and Yemen.

items.title: Mediator Pakistan says US-Iran talks ongoing as foes trade attacks
items.summary: TEHERAN: Mediator Pakistan insisted on Thursday that negotiations between Iran and the United States were ongoing, even as Washington carried out a "heavy wave of strikes" on its foe in retaliation for fresh attacks targeting Jordan. On Thursday, Jordan reported intercepting Iranian missiles for a second day running, while Kuwait said an Iranian strike that hit a building belonging to a Chinese company killed one person. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday that two oil tankers attempting to transit the strait with US support turned back after one of them caught fire.

items.title: US Treasury anti-money laundering chief Gacki to join Citi as global head of sanctions
items.summary: UNITED STATES: The US Treasury on Thursday said the director of its anti-money laundering Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), Andrea Gacki, was stepping down to join Citigroup as the bank's global head of sanctions. Gacki is leaving government service after 25 years at the Treasury and the Department of Justice and will remain at FinCEN for several weeks to support a smooth leadership transition, the Treasury said. The Treasury said Casanova previously worked on FinCEN enforcement actions, helping lead the case that resulted in a record US$1.3 billion Treasury fine against TD Bank.

items.title: 'Use Adibah Amin's works in schools to foster unity'
items.summary: The Universiti Malaya pro-chancellor said Adibah's writings remained highly relevant as Malaysia continued to navigate issues of race, religion and social cohesion. Adibah's 'As I Was Passing' belongs squarely to the latter," she said. Monash University Malaysia president and Pro Vice-Chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Adeeba Kamarulzaman said the university was pleased to celebrate Adibah's work alongside Malaysia's rich literary and cultural heritage.

items.title: MACC recommends AI scanners at cargo terminals to strengthen dangerous goods checks
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 30 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has submitted several improvement recommendations to the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) to strengthen the management of dangerous goods (DG), following a governance investigation related to the incident at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport. The approval of the recommendation was formalised through the signing of the Governance Improvement Report by CAAM deputy chief executive officer Captain Mohd Radzi Mohamad Alias and MACC BPT director Datuk Mohd Zaki Hassan. The report was presented by MACC BPT deputy director II Ahmad Shukri Mohamad Taib.

items.title: Workplace mental health policy draft expected by October, says health minister
items.summary: REMBAU, July 30 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) aims to finalise the workplace mental health policy draft by September or October, once engagement sessions with ministries, agencies and other stakeholders are completed. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the engagement sessions would involve the Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma), the Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH), the Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) and the Malaysian Trades Union Congress (MTUC). He said the timeframe would allow the ministry to develop a comprehensive policy and guidelines aimed at creating a conducive, safe and harmonious working environment.

items.title: High Court acquits preacher Fathi Na’im of rape, sexual assault charges
items.summary: KLANG, July 30 — The High Court has acquitted and discharged independent preacher Muhammad Fathi Na’im Mazlam of three charges of rape and sexual assault involving a 13-year-old girl, allegedly committed five years ago. Judge Roszianayati Ahmad delivered the decision yesterday after allowing the 34-year-old’s appeal to set aside his conviction and sentence imposed by the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court last year. The High Court ruled that the Sessions Court had erred in refusing an application to adjourn the trial to allow the appellant to obtain legal representation.

items.title: N. Sembilan polls: Anwar touts Pakatan manifesto as blueprint for continued state development
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 30 — Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) manifesto for the Negeri Sembilan state election reflects the coalition’s commitment to continuing the state’s stable, progressive and inclusive development agenda for the well-being of all its people, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. On July 20, PH launched its manifesto themed “Negeri Sembilan Kekal Harapan” (Negeri Sembilan Stays With Harapan), outlining 10 key commitments as its pledge to voters in the state election. Anwar, who is also PKR president, appealed to the people of Negeri Sembilan to continue placing their trust in PH.

items.title: Kluang newborn death: Post-mortem confirms baby died from multiple stab wounds
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, July 30 — Police have confirmed that a newborn baby girl found in a toilet bowl at a terrace house used as a hostel for college students in Kluang yesterday died from multiple stab wounds to the chest. Initial investigations found that the baby girl was discovered by a lecturer in the toilet bowl of the rented house. The student gave birth to another baby girl at the hospital after doctors discovered a second baby (a twin) in her womb.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI report: AGC to assess findings for possible prosecution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) will immediately review the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into the management and operations of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) from 2014 to 2020. The AGC also welcomed the Cabinet’s decision to make the RCI report public and said it viewed seriously the findings relating to TH’s management, investments and allegations of misconduct contained in the report. The AGC urged the public to refrain from speculation, making assumptions or disseminating unverified information that could jeopardise ongoing investigations and undermine confidence in Lembaga Tabung Haji’s ability to carry out its responsibilities under the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535).

items.title: Lawyer: Anwar will sue for defamation if PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim fails to respond in 48 hours
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will sue PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man over the latter’s alleged defamatory remarks, if the PAS leader fails to respond within 48 hours to a legal letter sent out today, Anwar’s lawyer has said. Anwar’s lawyer Datuk Sankara Narayan Nair said he had acted on Anwar’s instructions to issue a letter of demand today to Tuan Ibrahim over a “series of allegedly defamatory statements made outside Parliament on June 14, 2026 against the prime minister and subsequently republished on social media”. He said the letter had also demanded Tuan Ibrahim to pay compensation and legal costs.

items.title: ‘This is even fancier than the PM’s office’: Anwar launches Maybank’s new headquarters at Menara Merdeka Maybank
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today officially launched Maybank’s new headquarters at the Menara Merdeka Maybank. Menara Merdeka Maybank, formerly known as Merdeka 118, is the world’s second-tallest building, with the bank’s headquarters occupying the 70th floor. “Menara Merdeka Maybank is more than our new headquarters.

items.title: MCMC, LLM sign MoU to boost highway communications infrastructure
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, July 30 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) today signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen strategic cooperation in developing communications infrastructure along the nation’s highway network. The MoU aims to accelerate digital infrastructure development alongside physical infrastructure to improve telecommunications coverage and service quality while supporting national economic growth. Also present were Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching, Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Works Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Azman Ibrahim.

items.title: MACC forms special task force to review and examine Tabung Haji RCI report
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 30 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has set up a special task force to review and examine the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji, which was made public on Tuesday. MACC said the review would focus on possible elements of corruption, criminal breach of trust, document forgery, abuse of power and money laundering under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009, the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001, as well as other related laws. It said the commission was committed to ensuring that every issue highlighted in the RCI report was thoroughly examined.

items.title: Penang JPJ issues 1,328 summonses to foreign drivers under Ops PeWA since Jan 1
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, July 30 — The Penang Road Transport Department (JPJ) has issued 1,328 summonses to foreign drivers for various offences and impounded 178 vehicles under Op Khas Pemandu Warga Asing (PeWA) conducted since January 1. State JPJ director Zulkifly Ismail said that as of today, a total of 19,239 vehicles driven by foreigners were inspected, with enforcement action taken against 638 vehicles. “The operation is aimed at curbing offences involving foreign drivers who drive or operate motor vehicles without the required qualification, namely a valid driving licence.

items.title: Malaysia highways to get 77 new telecommunications towers to improve coverage, says works minister
items.summary: He said the target was among the outcomes of the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed today between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) to strengthen communications infrastructure along the country’s highway network. “In this context, cooperation between LLM and MCMC is crucial because the development of smart highways requires strong coordination between road infrastructure and communications infrastructure. Earlier, MCMC and LLM signed the MoU to strengthen strategic cooperation in developing communications infrastructure along the national highway network.

items.title: Penang’s Jalan Magazine to close for three days from Aug 7 for LRT works
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 30 — A section of Jalan Magazine towards Lebuh Carnarvon near Komtar here will be closed in stages for three days from August 7 to facilitate utility relocation works for the Light Rail Transit (LRT) Mutiara Line Project. According to a Penang Mutiara Line (PML) project statement today, the closure will take place from 10pm on Friday (August 7) until 5am on Monday (August 10), involving three lanes between the Capri Hotel and The Magazine Hotel construction areas. The closure is required for preliminary works under the LRT Mutiara Line Project Package CMC1, involving utility relocation by the Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP).

items.title: Starlink to trial satellite-to-phone internet service in Malaysia, says Fahmi
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, July 30 — Satellite internet provider Starlink plans to conduct a trial of its direct-to-device (D2D), or direct-to-cell, technology in Malaysia, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said the technology has the potential to deliver internet connectivity directly to mobile phones via satellite in selected areas without relying on telecommunications towers. Also present were Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi, Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching, Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Works Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Azman Ibrahim.

items.title: Zayn Rayyan case: High Court to hear mother Ismanira’s appeal against five-year jail term on Aug 19
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 30 — The High Court today set August 19 to hear Ismanira Abdul Manaf’s appeal against her conviction and five-year prison sentence for neglecting her six-year-old son, Zayn Rayyan Abdul Matin, resulting in physical injury three years ago. Judge Noor Hisham Ismail set the date after deputy public prosecutor Raja Zaizul Faridah Raja Zaharudin informed the court that the prosecution required time to file further submissions in response to the defence’s additional arguments. Counsel Haresh Mahadevan, representing Ismanira, raised no objection.

items.title: Driver charged with murder over Teluk Intan crash killing two teenage schoolgirls
items.summary: TELUK INTAN, July 30 — The car driver involved in a road crash that claimed the lives of two teenage girls on Jalan Padang Tembak here last Sunday was charged in the Magistrates’ Court today with four offences, including two counts of murder. Under the first charge, Alex is accused of murdering 17-year-old Nur Dania Arissa Salim near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Seri Setia on Jalan Padang Tembak at 6.35pm on July 26. The second charge alleges that he murdered 16-year-old Nur Atikah Abdullah at the same location, date and time.

items.title: Special Parliament sitting on Tabung Haji RCI report set for Aug 11, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim revealed that the special parliamentary sitting on Tabung Haji’s Royal Commision of Inquiry (RCI) report will be held on August 11. “A special parliamentary session will be held this August 11. “The session will begin from 10am until the evening,” Anwar said.

items.title: Committee overseeing haj operations needs statutory status, says Tabung Haji RCI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has recommended that the Haj Affairs Committee be given statutory status under the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535) and assigned specific responsibilities. According to the RCI report released yesterday, the committee was established to assess and decide on matters relating to haj operations after the Haj Advisory Council was dissolved in 2018 following the repeal of the Tabung Haji Board Act 1969 (Act 8). The RCI proposed that the Haj Affairs Committee advise the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) on policies and planning related to haj affairs, as well as deliberate on issues concerning the welfare of pilgrims and other matters referred to it in relation to haj operations.

items.title: Home Ministry starts refugee checks as Malaysia prepares to send back 5,000 Myanmar nationals
items.summary: BUKIT KAYU HITAM, July 30 — The Home Ministry (KDN) has begun identifying, documenting and screening Rohingya refugees as part of preparations to repatriate 5,000 Myanmar nationals after the Myanmar government agreed to accept the return of its citizens currently in Malaysia. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the process was being carried out through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) in line with National Security Council (MKN) Directive No. He said the DPP process involved several stages, including tracing, identification, security screening and determining the status of each individual before confirmation documents were issued.

items.title: As polling day nears, what’s on Negeri Sembilan voters’ minds?
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 30 — Over the past decade, Aina Mohamed, 33, has watched Negeri Sembilan evolve, with new public facilities, businesses and housing developments changing parts of the state that once felt much quieter. The Negeri Sembilan native, who lives in Ampangan, said the changes were easy to spot, from the opening of the Urban Transformation Centre (UTC) and new commercial areas to the transformation of towns across the state. Alongside the state’s physical growth, she said she had also noticed changes in how communities interact.

items.title: Love scams and fake investments cost Terengganu RM21m in first half of 2026
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, July 30 — Terengganu continues to record an increase in commercial crime cases, with 1,009 cases recorded in the first six months of this year compared to 995 cases during the same period last year. Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said cybercrime accounted for the highest number of cases at 980; followed by counterfeit currency (13 cases); offences under the Moneylenders Act 1951 (Amendment 2011) (12 cases); criminal breach of trust (three cases); and other cases (one case). He said that commercial crime cases this year also recorded an increase in total losses, rising from RM20,198,493.73 between January and June last year to RM21,035,250.57 during the same period this year.

items.title: Heart op recovery keeps Najib from court in bid to revive suit against ex-AG Thomas, but majority grants delay — with a warning
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 30 — In a 2-1 majority decision, the Apex Court today granted Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak’s application to adjourn the hearing of his leave bid to revive his RM1.9 million civil suit against former Attorney-General (AG) Tan Sri Tommy Thomas after being told that the former prime minister was recovering from a heart procedure. A three-member panel comprising Federal Court judges Datuk Seri Abu Bakar Jais and Datuk Azmi Ariffin formed the majority, while Justice Datuk Azimah Omar dissented. “Najib is unwell and, under the circumstances, I am allowing this application,” he said.

items.title: Sabah sets aside RM100m for scholarships, targets future healthcare talent
items.summary: Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Haji Noor said the Sabah State Government Scholarship (BKNS) allocation will cover existing recipients as well as new sponsorships for 2026, involving 2,182 students, with emphasis on strategic fields including science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM). Hajiji, who is also chairman of the Yayasan Sabah board of trustees, said education remained a priority for the state government as the foundation for producing skilled and competitive human capital. He said the government had also expanded other education assistance programmes, including the Sabah State Government Excellent Scholarship, the B40 and Rural Programme Scholarship, as well as financial aid schemes aimed at easing the burden of higher education costs.

items.title: Pakatan demands accountability over Tabung Haji misconduct, calls to prosecute without compromise
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 30 — The government must act swiftly to restore public confidence in Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) and safeguard the rights of depositors following the release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into the pilgrim fund, Pakatan Harapan (PH) said. “PH commends the government for releasing the Tabung Haji RCI report, which clearly demonstrates its continued commitment to good governance, accountability and transparency,” he said in a statement today. Saifuddin said the government under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had successfully restored TH’s financial management, noting that 75 per cent of the RCI’s recommendations had already been implemented.

items.title: RCI pushes for new Haj Fund dept to safeguard Tabung Haji’s future as deposits approach RM100b
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has recommended the establishment of a dedicated department known as the Haj Fund under TH to manage depositors’ funds, with oversight by the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) to enhance investment management professionalism. The RCI said the move would allow TH to retain its investment management functions rather than be placed under a separate subsidiary. The TH Board would appoint senior officers, including the chief investment officer, who would be supervised by the SC.

items.title: Abdul Azeez says ready to face fresh probe over Tabung Haji RCI findings
items.summary: JELEBU, July 30 — Former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim said he is prepared to be investigated again if necessary following allegations of misconduct raised in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report, according to Sinar Harian. Abdul Azeez said the 204-page RCI report had been completed at the end of 2022 and tabled at several Cabinet meetings. Abdul Azeez said he had previously appealed to then prime minister Dr Mahathir, then deputy prime minister Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail and former minister in the Prime Minister’s Department Datuk Seri Mujahid Yusof Rawa to establish an RCI into the matter.

items.title: Are Malaysia’s small traders ready for Asean’s digital economy? Yes, even fried banana sellers use QR codes, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — Malaysia's micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) are well positioned to tap Asean's 680-million-consumer market under the proposed Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA), supported by their high level of digital adoption, Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said. He said harmonising digital regulatory frameworks would reduce market fragmentation, creating a more efficient, cost-effective and globally competitive Asean digital economic bloc. Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin is confident that Malaysia’s micro, small and medium enterprises are ready for Asean’s cross-border digital trade.

items.title: RM1,000 subsidy and a new centre: How Malaysia is stepping up support for kids with autism as registrations rise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — About 93,000 of the 850,000 persons with disabilities (PwDs) registered with the Department of Social Welfare (JKM) as of June this year are those with autism, the Dewan Negara was told today. Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying said the increase in registrations had prompted the government to enhance various initiatives on early intervention, education and skills training for the group. “Recently, the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) established an Autism Service Centre in Bangi with the primary objective of providing a one-stop centre offering quality, affordable and easily accessible services,” she said when replying to a question from Senator Dr A. Lingeshwaran.

items.title: Agriculture Ministry says Malaysia imports too much ginger, mangoes, rice and fresh milk — here’s what’s changing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) is focusing on increasing the production of agri-food commodities with low Self-Sufficiency Ratio (SSR) levels to reduce the country’s dependence on food imports. Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said commodities that still require attention include ginger, with an SSR of 15.5 per cent, mangoes (20 per cent), rice (about 52 per cent) and fresh milk (66.7 per cent). Meanwhile, in response to concerns over food supply to rural areas in Sabah and Sarawak, Chan said KPKM is working with PLANMalaysia to develop the National Food Source Area Land Use Planning Master Plan to safeguard food production areas.
